chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'When a man has a concubine and he frees her, what is her ruling?' He said, 'It is not permissible for her to marry until her waiting period (iddah) of three months has elapsed. If her master dies, her waiting period is four months and ten days.'
ai.seo_question: What is the iddah (waiting period) for a freed concubine in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinct legal status of a concubine (*surriyyah*) upon manumission, establishing a three-month waiting period that parallels the *iddah* of divorce rather than death. It further specifies that if the owner dies while she is still in his possession, her waiting period extends to four months and ten days, demonstrating the juristic principle that manumission does not immediately sever the marital bond but requires a period of observance to ensure lineage clarity. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the eligibility of freed concubines to remarry.
